name: Mana Vault
oracle_text:
This artifact doesn't untap during your untap step.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may pay {4}. If you do, untap this artifact.
At the beginning of your draw step, if this artifact is tapped, it deals 1 damage to you.
{T}: Add {C}{C}{C}.
blocked_sentences: This artifact doesn't untap during your untap step.

needs.what: a static effect -- say `skip_untap_step` -- that a permanent prints on itself (and, with a filter, on others: Winter Orb, Kismet, Stasis-likes) meaning "doesn't untap during its controller's untap step", read by the untap step alongside `skip_next_untap` and `frozen_by`. It must be a printed characteristic with no lifetime of its own: it holds for exactly as long as the ability is on the battlefield, is spent by nothing, and must not fight `skip_next_untap` (the untap step must not consume that one-shot on a permanent already held by the static), while leaving explicit `untap` effects -- Mana Vault's own upkeep payment -- free to untap it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `static_effects` carries `untap_during_each_untap_step`, the exact inverse, and nothing that suppresses untapping; `characteristics.untap_also` is the only untap-related static reader and it only adds permanents to the untap set. The two engine fields that do suppress untapping are both written by resolution, not by a printed static: `skip_untap` sets `skip_next_untap`, which `primitives.untap_all` clears in the very untap step it skips (a one-shot -- it would hold Mana Vault for one turn and release it on the next), and `freeze` sets `frozen_by` to the source oid for its source's lifetime. Both are `ops`, so the only way to reach either is to invent a triggered ability (`self_enters` + `freeze` on `self_only`) to carry a line that is printed as a static -- which the residual gate would see as a triggered ability claiming a static sentence, and which would additionally sit on the stack, be responded to, and be re-installed on every re-entry rather than simply being true while the artifact is on the battlefield.
